course_title: Short Term Mine Planning and Scheduling

learning_outcomes.description: Assess the context in which they are to undertake an execution plan with consideration and compliance to technical, environmental and social variables.
Hypothesise, test, and validate a critical path to improve mining production.
Communicate the decision-making process in relevant mining contexts to empower operations and other stakeholders.
Develop and justify contingency plans to provide alternative paths to achieve the main objective of the mine execution plan.
Identify and use appropriate project management tools and strategies to develop and evaluate an execution plan.
Visualise the critical path of key production milestones to various stakeholders using appropriate software tools.
Apply appropriate mathematical techniques in the decision-making process to inform the critical path.
Reflect on mining project plans and industry practitioners to derive future consideration for professional practice.

assessments.task_description:
This component involves the review and selection of the operational setting (eg. blast block at your operation) for the purpose of generating a short term mine plan and schedule. If you are not in an operational setting, a case study may be made available. You will be required to submit a pitch presentation that goes some way in collating the information and inputs required as the basis in the development of your short-term schedule/plan. Please refer to Blackboard for detailed marking criteria.

This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI and/or MT technologies, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which artificial intelligence will provide only limited support and guidance.

A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct.

To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their written submission independent of AI and MT tools.

learning_activities.topic:
Module 1: Foundations of short-term planning and scheduling

The first module of this course introduces the key components of the short-term planning and scheduling process and its role within the broader mine planning process and mining value chain. The objective of short-term scheduling, the time horizons involved, and general resource and sequencing constraints are discussed.

Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04, L08

learning_activities.topic:
Module 2: Gantt Charts

Module 2 introduces Gantt Charts. Gantt Charts are a very common way of communicating plans and schedules - not just in mining but across a range of industries. This is followed by a section on Critical Paths.

Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04, L05, L06, L07, L08
learning_activities.topic_description: Module 2: Gantt Charts Module 2 introduces Gantt Charts. Gantt Charts are a very common way of communicating plans and schedules - not just in mining but across a range of industries. This is followed by a section on Critical Paths.

learning_activities.topic:
Module 3: Critical path

This module introduces Network Diagrams and Critical Path Method (CPM). Strategies to potentially reduce completion times across a given schedule are addressed.

Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04, L05, L06, L07
learning_activities.topic_description: Module 3: Critical path This module introduces Network Diagrams and Critical Path Method (CPM). Strategies to potentially reduce completion times across a given schedule are addressed.

learning_activities.topic:
Module 4: Introduction to mathematical optimisation

The focus of this module is to further enhance a mine planner's decision-making capability by introducing mathematical optimisation concepts which often form the basis for many of the computerised planning tools that are commercially available.

Learning outcomes: L02, L05, L06, L07
learning_activities.topic_description: Module 4: Introduction to mathematical optimisation The focus of this module is to further enhance a mine planner's decision-making capability by introducing mathematical optimisation concepts which often form the basis for many of the computerised planning tools that are commercially available.

learning_activities.topic:
Module 5: Mathematical optimisation

The focus of this module is on the developing Linear Programming (LP) and Mixed Integer Programming (MIP) models to aid in the solution of complex mining related scheduling problems.

Learning outcomes: L02, L05, L06, L07
